department: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences

deadline.value: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, typically within 4-6 weeks of submission.
deadline.quote: We will try and notify you within 4-6 weeks of your application. However, due to various funding applications and deadlines, you may not receive an answer during this timeframe.

entry_route.value: Standard entry requires a bachelor's honours degree at Upper Second class (2:1) or above, or a Lower Second class (2:2) bachelor's with a taught master's completed at Merit level.
entry_route.quote:
To be considered for entry to our standard PhD programmes, you'll typically require at least:
a bachelor's degree with honours, Upper Second class (2:1) or above (or international equivalent) in a relevant subject area.
Candidates who hold a Lower Second class (2:2) bachelor's honours degree (or international equivalent) may also be considered if they can demonstrate:
evidence of academic progress through a taught master’s degree, completed at a minimum grade of Merit (or international equivalent).

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact their prospective project supervisor and discuss their suitability prior to applying.
supervisor.quote: Contacted the project supervisor and spoken to them about your suitability for the project.

funding.value: Applicants nominated by their supervisor for funding may be invited to further interviews to determine suitability.
funding.quote: If you are nominated for funding by your supervisor, you may be invited to further interviews to determine your suitability for funding.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: Postgraduate research degree (Earth Sciences PhD) in the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Manchester.
